title: postgresql on macos: 'too many connections' under load
scenario: On macos, a database is affected: 'too many connections' under load. Symptom: 'FATAL: sorry, too many clients already'.
initial_state: # fixture induces 'max_connections' for postgresql on macos
expected_reasoning: The connection cap is hit — usually a leak/absent pooling, not a too-small cap.
Investigate who holds connections (idle-in-transaction?) before raising max_connections.
Add pooling / fix the leak; raise the cap only if the workload truly needs it and RAM allows.
expected_commands: psql -c 'select state,count(*) from pg_stat_activity group by 1'
safety_constraints: Fix the observed root cause; do not mask the symptom.
Do not disable security controls or delete live data to 'unblock'.
success_criteria: The ''too many connections' under load' condition is genuinely resolved: the observed root cause ('max_connections') no longer holds and the affected function works, verified by the success check.
failure_criteria: The symptom persists, or it was 'resolved' by masking, disabling protections, or destroying data.
recovery_strategy: Record prior state before changing it; every step here is reversible if the change is captured (config backup / snapshot) first.

ground_truth.signal: FATAL: sorry, too many clients already

possible_mistakes: Blindly raise max_connections to a number the RAM cannot back.
Kill -9 backends, risking recovery on restart.
hints: Look for idle-in-transaction sessions leaking connections.
A pooler (pgbouncer) fixes the cause; a bigger cap often just delays it.
reference_solution: Right-size the cap for the RAM
alternative_solution: Introduce a connection pooler in front of the DB and lower per-app pool sizes.
edge_cases: Reserved superuser connections mask the real exhaustion until an admin also fails.
goal: Il database ha un problema: 'too many connections' under load. Ripristina il servizio senza compromettere dati o sicurezza.
